import sys, json

# The incoming message and this cell's OWN configuration arrive on the same
# stdin document: `params` is one of its three top-level objects, beside
# `envelope` and `body`, and the substrate always sets it ({} when there is
# nothing to hand over). Every knob below is read from it, so each one is
# per-INSTANCE configuration -- the surface and the core of one agent classify
# their tools apart, which the colony-wide environment form could not say at
# all. The literal beside each name is the shipped default; it is the same value
# the template config and `contract.settings` carry, and a test pins the three
# against each other.
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc["body"]
envelope = doc["envelope"]
P = doc.get("params") or {}


def _knob(key, default):
    v = P.get(key, default)
    # A knob explicitly set to null or to whitespace is "not configured", not a
    # crash: an operator who blanks a line in a config means the default.
    return default if v is None else v


def _int(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        return default
    return int(v)


def _str(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    return "" if v is None else str(v)


def _list(key, default):
    """A declared name list. A mutation writes it as a JSON array
    (`["consult_cogny", "remember"]`); a comma string is read the same way,
    because that is the shape the knob had when it was an environment line and
    the shape somebody types into a config. Anything else is EMPTY rather than
    half-read -- a declaration that lost half its names would leave a fan-in
    waiting for a call that never answers, with nobody saying so."""
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str):
        v = v.split(",")
    if not isinstance(v, list):
        return []
    return [str(n).strip() for n in v if str(n).strip()]


# --- per-answer call budget ------------------------------------------------
# One brain answer may carry N calls in ONE bundle. The ITERATION cap lives at
# the seam that starts a round (the collector); the CALL cap lives here,
# because only this cell ever sees the whole bundle.
MAX_CALLS = _int("max_calls", 16)
# --- the async tool class (GH #28, R-CG-3) ---------------------------------
# Some tools do not answer inside a round. An advisor that THINKS comes back
# minutes later, on a lane of its own -- and a fan-in that waits for it would
# be racing its own idle window instead of ending the turn. Naming such a tool
# HERE is the one declaration: this cell is the only one that ever sees the
# whole bundle, so it is the only one that can classify a call. The call still
# travels the ordinary way; what travels with it is the marker.
ASYNC_TOOLS = set(_list("async_tools", ""))
# --- the handoff class (GH #372) -------------------------------------------
# A STRONGER form of async, and the difference is the turn: an async call does
# not answer inside the round; a HANDOFF call takes the turn with it, because
# the answer will come from a later turn -- an advisor's event arriving on its
# own lane, an escalation re-entering the seam as a fresh assembly. The round it
# leaves behind is therefore over even when no sentence stood beside it.
#
# Everything else in the async class is fire-and-forget: `remember` writes and
# never comes back, and the model still owes THIS turn an answer. Told apart
# nowhere else, a bundle of one bare `remember` call ended the turn in silence --
# no interim, no final, no error (measured: three of five harness runs). Which
# of the two a tool is, is tool semantics, so it is DECLARED, in the one cell
# that sees the whole bundle and already classifies. A handoff tool is async by
# definition, so naming it here is enough -- the union below is the whole of it.
HANDOFF_TOOLS = set(_list("handoff_tools", ""))
ASYNC_TOOLS |= HANDOFF_TOOLS
# --- the interim class (GH #539) -------------------------------------------
# A sentence standing beside a bundle is an INTERIM answer, and interim is a
# promise made to a CHANNEL: the user reads this now, the real answer follows.
# A brain WITHOUT a channel has nowhere to put such a sentence. An advisor
# core's answer lane IS the advice lane of the voice that asked it, so an
# interim arriving there is filed as the advice it is not -- and the voice
# verbalises it, and sometimes asks again, and the core answers with the next
# interim (measured on a live colony: 11 of 26 answers one core put on that
# lane were interim, and all 11 arrived as advice).
#
# Whether the brain behind this cell has a channel cannot be read off a bundle,
# so it is DECLARED -- in the same cell that already declares the async and the
# handoff class, for the same reason: this is the only cell that sees the whole
# bundle, and a sentence beside it is part of that bundle. Default ON, so every
# wiring that exists keeps the behaviour it has. It reads from `params`, not
# from an environment token -- and since dispatcher@1.2.0 its three neighbours
# are read the same way (GH #138).
INTERIM = _str("interim", "1").strip().lower() not in ("", "0", "false", "no")
hop = (envelope.get("header") or {}).get("hop") or {}
CTX = (envelope.get("header") or {}).get("context") or {}
finish = str(hop.get("finish_reason", "") or "")
# --- the window a result is read in (GH #1085, R-IG-1) ----------------------
# A tool cuts its result to a share of the window of the model that reads it
# and learns that window from `input_soft`: in `context` where a curator set
# it, else on the hop. The brain stamps its catalogue row's `input_soft` on
# every answer, a tool-call bundle included -- but a hop lives for one
# emission, and this cell emits anew. Without the line below the stamp ended
# here and every tool behind a dispatcher answered whole, up to the carrier
# ceiling (review I-1 of the strand that took the tools' fixed 256 KiB away).
# The brain that asked is the brain that reads the result, so ITS window rides
# on with each call, unchanged; nothing else of the brain's hop does.
_soft = hop.get("input_soft")
WINDOW = (_soft if isinstance(_soft, (int, float)) and not isinstance(_soft, bool)
          and _soft > 0 else None)
msgs = d.get("messages", [])
calls = [m for m in msgs if m.get("type") == "tool_call"]


def emit(out):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(out))
    sys.exit(0)


def error_result(call_id, text, code):
    """A synthetic tool_result in place of a call that will never run. It keeps
    the original tool_call_id, so the round stays fan-in-complete: the brain
    sees the failure and has to answer it instead of waiting for it. Dropping
    the call silently would stall the fan-in until the TTL runs out, and TTL
    expiry emits nothing at all towards the surface."""
    return {"header": {"route": "result", "tool_call_id": call_id, "error_code": code},
            "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": call_id,
                          "text": text}]}


def parts_of(call, i):
    """(id, name, raw arguments) of one OpenAI-form tool_call turn, whose text
    is the stringified function object. `name` is None when the turn cannot be
    read that way -- an unroutable call, not a tool."""
    call_id = str(call.get("id") or "call-%d" % i)
    try:
        fn = json.loads(call.get("text") or "{}")
    except Exception:
        return call_id, None, None
    if not isinstance(fn, dict) or not fn.get("name"):
        return call_id, None, None
    args = fn.get("arguments", "{}")
    if not isinstance(args, str):
        args = json.dumps(args)
    return call_id, str(fn["name"]), args


# --- family calls (GH #1245) ----------------------------------------------
# A collector that folds its menu shows the model ONE tool per family, `F` with
# `{op, args}`, while every answerer behind this cell stays flat and keeps its
# single-op name. This cell names the tool on every call it lets go, so it is the
# one place that unfolds: `F{op, args}` leaves as `F_op` carrying `args` alone,
# and nothing downstream learns that a fold existed -- the rights an answerer
# checks per op, the presenter's `tool_name`, a run proof reading `file_replace`
# all see what they saw before. `{op, args}` -- `args` an object, other keys
# beside the two dropped -- or `{op}` alone, as `{op, args: {}}` (GH #1260),
# unfolds, and only under the name of a family the collector folded. The shape
# alone proves nothing (GH #1260): a tool outside the fold may take an `op` and
# an `args` object of its own -- an orga `propose {item, op, args, why}` does --
# and unfolding it would rename it to an answerer nobody runs. Unfolding runs
# before the async and the handoff class are read, because both are declared
# for the single op, not for the family.
#
# Which names are families this cell cannot see: it never sees the menu. The
# collector writes the fold and names its families on every `curate` seam
# (`hop.tools_folded`), the composite's curate edge lifts them into the context,
# and the context rides the brain's answer to this cell. No fold, no name, and
# nothing unfolds.
FOLDED = {n.strip() for n in str(CTX.get("tools_folded", "") or "").split(",")
          if n.strip()}

# GH #1272 (K3): the op tools the collector keeps at hint level
# (`hint_own_op`, named on the seam as `hop.tools_hinted` and lifted beside
# `tools_folded`). The model saw a name, a line and `{op}`; its `help` has no
# answerer either and comes back the same way, the tool's name in `help_for`.
# Every other op of such a tool leaves for its answerer as it came.
HINTED = {n.strip() for n in str(CTX.get("tools_hinted", "") or "").split(",")
          if n.strip()}

# `op: "help"` asks about the family itself and has no answerer to go to. It
# comes back at once on the result lane, the family in `help_for` and the
# request (`args`) as its text; the collector answers it from its menu store.
HELP = {}


def unfold(call_id, name, args):
    """(id, name, args) of one call after the family rule: `F_op` and the inner
    `args` for a family call, the call unchanged for everything else."""
    if name is not None and name in HINTED and name not in FOLDED:
        try:
            a = json.loads(args or "{}")
        except Exception:
            return call_id, name, args
        if isinstance(a, dict) and a.get("op") == "help":
            HELP[call_id] = name
            return call_id, name, json.dumps(dict((k, v) for k, v in a.items() if k != "op"))
        return call_id, name, args
    if name is None or name not in FOLDED:
        return call_id, name, args
    try:
        a = json.loads(args or "{}")
    except Exception:
        return call_id, name, args
    # OR-WG-4 (GH #1260): `{op}` ALONE is a family call too. The hint level of
    # a family (`tool_scope.hint`) shows the model the schema `{op}` and
    # nothing else, so every call made under it arrived without `args`, left
    # as tool `F` and dead-lettered -- `help` among them, the one call the
    # hint level exists to make. Alone means alone: `{op}` beside other keys
    # is still a tool with an `op` of its own.
    if isinstance(a, dict) and set(a) == {"op"}:
        a = {"op": a["op"], "args": {}}
    # GH #1260: `args` is the family's own key, so under a folded name `op`
    # beside an `args` object is a family call whatever else rides along. A lab run
    # logged `web {op: search, args: {query}, id: "1"}`: with only EXACTLY
    # `{op, args}` unfolding it left as tool `web`, the tools hive answered
    # `unknown_tool` and the turn went without its search. The stray keys are
    # outside the family's schema and stay behind; only `args` travels.
    if not (isinstance(a, dict) and {"op", "args"} <= set(a)
            and isinstance(a["op"], str) and a["op"].strip()
            and isinstance(a["args"], dict)):
        return call_id, name, args
    op = a["op"].strip()
    # What stays behind is said, never lost in silence (GH #1260): a key the
    # model put beside `op` and `args` may have been meant as a parameter
    # (`web {op: search, args: {}, query}`), and the retry the answerer's
    # `invalid_input` asks for is read best beside this line.
    stray = sorted(k for k in a if k not in ("op", "args"))
    if stray:
        sys.stderr.write("dispatcher: family call %s (`%s`) dropped key(s) beside op and"
                         " args: %s\n" % (call_id, name, ", ".join(stray)))
    if op == "help":
        HELP[call_id] = name
    return call_id, "%s_%s" % (name, op), json.dumps(a["args"])


def help_result(call_id, family, args):
    """A help call answered in place, on the lane a refused call takes: the
    round stays fan-in-complete, and `help_for` names the family whose menu the
    collector answers from. Not an error, so no `error_code`."""
    return {"header": {"route": "result", "tool_call_id": call_id, "help_for": family},
            "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": call_id,
                          "text": args}]}


def async_keys(call_id, args):
    """The hop keys an async call carries. `consult_id` correlates the whole
    exchange: a FRESH consult is named by the call that opened it, a REPLY to a
    question the advisor asked back passes the id it was shown -- so the
    advisor keeps one thread instead of guessing which of its questions was
    answered. `consult_eta` is the model's own coarse duration estimate,
    produced in the SAME turn (GH #123): it is logged and nothing reads it."""
    try:
        a = json.loads(args or "{}")
    except Exception:
        a = {}
    if not isinstance(a, dict):
        a = {}
    return {"async": "1", "consult_id": str(a.get("consult_id") or call_id),
            "consult_eta": str(a.get("eta", "") or "")}


if not calls:
    # No bundle. The final answer travels; anything else stops here. The llm
    # error path echoes the INPUT conversation back with finish_reason "error",
    # and putting that on the answer lane would file the prompt as the agent's
    # own words -- an error lane belongs on the brain's edge, not in this cell.
    #
    # `length` travels as well (GH #842, OR-SN-3): a completion cut by
    # `max_tokens` -- reasoning that ate the budget, for example -- is the
    # model's own partial text, not an echo, and until 1.2.1 it left NOTHING
    # here: no answer, no error, no stderr line, which from the outside is a
    # hang. The reason rides on the hop, so whatever reads the answer can mark
    # it as cut (the collector stamps `truncated`, GH #843). Everything else
    # stays terminal -- `content_filter` and `error` belong to the brain's
    # error edge -- but it is said on stderr, never silent.
    if finish in ("stop", "length"):
        ans = {"header": {"route": "answer", "finish_reason": finish}, "messages": msgs}
        # GH #1260 (OR-WG-6): a sentence its caller marked interim -- the
        # bridge beside a required tool call (`context.interim`, the curator's
        # `hop.interim` lifted by the composite's edge) -- promises the answer
        # that follows in the same round. As a final answer it ended the round
        # at the fan-in before the tool result came back.
        # GH #1260 (OR-WG-9): the REQUIRED call of a tool round
        # (`context.interim` "tool") answered without its call. Not said --
        # on the fast way such prose made the weather up (lab r026c) -- and
        # not the round's end: the curator gives the round to the brain.
        if str(CTX.get("interim", "") or "") == "tool":
            sys.stderr.write("dispatcher: the required call of a tool round came back"
                             " without a call -- not said, the curator escalates\n")
            emit([])
        if str(CTX.get("interim", "") or "") == "1":
            # The knob holds here too (fix round 1, review M-2): `interim`
            # off says the brain behind this cell has no channel (GH #539),
            # and a promise nobody can read is not one -- the sentence does
            # not leave, and above all not as the round's final answer.
            if not INTERIM:
                sys.stderr.write("dispatcher: a sentence marked interim on a"
                                 " cell without a channel -- not said\n")
                emit([])
            ans["header"]["interim"] = "1"
        # The block a splitter cut out of this answer rides on (GH #871). This
        # cell rebuilds the answer it hands on, so a body slot it did not name
        # was dropped here -- and the collector behind it, which shows the model
        # its earlier answers, never got the block to show. Passed through as it
        # came, a string or nothing; this cell reads none of it.
        if isinstance(d.get("sidecar_raw"), str) and d["sidecar_raw"]:
            ans["sidecar_raw"] = d["sidecar_raw"]
        emit([ans])
    sys.stderr.write("dispatcher: finish '%s' without a tool call -- nothing"
                     " dispatched\n" % finish)
    emit([])

parsed = [unfold(*parts_of(c, i)) for i, c in enumerate(calls)]
async_ids = [cid for cid, name, _ in parsed if name in ASYNC_TOOLS]
handoff_ids = [cid for cid, name, _ in parsed if name in HANDOFF_TOOLS]

# PLAIN order: the expectation set FIRST, the calls after it. A tool that
# answers instantly must not reach the fan-in before the round exists there.
# `async_calls` rides on the same message: the fan-in is TOLD which ids it must
# not wait for, instead of keeping a second copy of the classification.
# `handoff_calls` rides beside `async_calls` and is always present, empty
# included: a hop key that is sometimes absent makes a CEL modifier fail, and a
# failed modifier skips the edge.
out = [{"header": {"route": "calls", "call_count": str(len(calls)),
                   "async_calls": ",".join(async_ids),
                   "handoff_calls": ",".join(handoff_ids)}, "messages": msgs}]

# Content AND tool_calls out of ONE response (R-CG-3, delta 1): a sentence next
# to the bundle belongs in the channel now, and the turn ends with it while the
# calls keep running. Asking a second inference for "one moment" is exactly the
# extra turn the advisor split abolishes.
#
# WHETHER IT IS INTERIM DEPENDS ON THE BUNDLE BESIDE IT (GH #378). This used to
# be marked `interim` unconditionally, and that stranded every turn of the
# shape an async tool description asks for -- 10 of 12 measured rounds under the
# shipped contract. `interim` is a promise that a final answer follows, so it is
# only true when something is still coming:
#
#   a NON-ASYNC call     the round re-enters the brain with its result, so a
#                        further answer is on its way        -> interim
#   a HANDOFF call       takes the turn with it; the answer arrives as a later
#                        turn                                -> interim
#   async, no handoff    fire-and-forget, and the model still owes THIS turn an
#                        answer -- the sentence IS it        -> FINAL
#
# So the sentence is final exactly when every call is async-and-not-handoff.
# That is the precise mirror of the fan-in's `acked and not waiting and over`:
# it files such a round as fired and never re-enters, which is correct -- what
# was wrong is that the only thing delivered had been labelled interim, so the
# turn carried an interim answer and no final one, forever.
said = [m for m in msgs
        if m.get("type") in ("text", None) and str(m.get("text", "") or "")]
if said:
    waited_for = [cid for cid, _, _ in parsed
                  if cid not in async_ids or cid in handoff_ids]
    header = {"route": "answer", "finish_reason": finish}
    if waited_for:
        header["interim"] = "1"
    # AND ONLY IF THERE IS SOMEWHERE TO SAY IT (GH #539). `INTERIM` off means
    # the brain behind this cell has no channel, and then the sentence does not
    # leave this cell at all -- not on the answer lane, and so not into the
    # window either, because the `calls` lane hands the fan-in the assistant
    # turn and the fan-in drops its text on the ground that the answer lane
    # wrote it. Both halves say the same thing: a sentence nobody could hear
    # was never said. The FINAL sentence still leaves whatever the knob says --
    # `waited_for` empty is the GH #378 case, where nothing is coming after it
    # and the sentence IS the answer this turn owes. What is withheld is only
    # the PROMISE of a later one, and a promise nobody can read is not one.
    if INTERIM or not waited_for:
        sentence = {"header": header, "messages": said}
        # The block the splitter shows beside this sentence rides on too (GH
        # #871 fix round 1): on a consult's return the sentence is an earlier
        # answer in the window, and a bare one there was the precedent the fix
        # removed everywhere else. Passed through as it came; read by nobody here.
        if isinstance(d.get("sidecar_raw"), str) and d["sidecar_raw"]:
            sentence["sidecar_raw"] = d["sidecar_raw"]
        out.append(sentence)

if len(calls) > MAX_CALLS:
    reason = "call budget exceeded: %d calls in one answer, limit %d" % (len(calls), MAX_CALLS)
    for call_id, _, _ in parsed:
        out.append(error_result(call_id, reason, "call_budget_exceeded"))
    emit(out)

for call_id, name, args in parsed:
    if name is None:
        out.append(error_result(call_id,
                                "malformed tool_call: text is not a JSON object with a name",
                                "malformed_tool_call"))
        continue
    if call_id in HELP:
        out.append(help_result(call_id, HELP[call_id], args))
        continue
    # No topology knowledge: this cell names the TOOL, an edge knows the CELL.
    header = {"route": "tool", "tool_name": name, "tool_call_id": call_id}
    if WINDOW is not None:
        header["input_soft"] = WINDOW
    if name in ASYNC_TOOLS:
        header.update(async_keys(call_id, args))
    out.append({"header": header,
                "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": call_id,
                              "text": args}]})
emit(out)
